title: 10 Common E-commerce Website Mistakes That Are Costing You Customers
description: Discover 10 common eCommerce website mistakes that may be costing your business customers and sales. Learn how to improve website speed, mobile experience, SEO, product pages, checkout and customer trust.
author: Sellaro Digitec Team
imageAlt: Business owner reviewing common eCommerce website mistakes and online store performance

content.text: Building an eCommerce website is only the first step towards running a successful online business. Your website also needs to attract visitors, provide a smooth shopping experience, build customer trust and make purchasing easy. However, many online stores unknowingly make mistakes that frustrate visitors and prevent them from completing purchases.

From slow loading speeds and confusing navigation to poorly optimized product pages and complicated checkout processes, even small website issues can affect how customers interact with your store. If your eCommerce website is receiving visitors but not generating the expected enquiries or sales, it may be time to review its performance.
In this guide, we explore 10 common eCommerce website mistakes that could be costing your business customers, along with practical ways to identify and fix them.
Key takeaways

items: Slow website loading speeds can frustrate visitors and increase the likelihood of them leaving.
A website that does not work properly on mobile devices can create unnecessary barriers for shoppers.
Poor navigation and confusing product categories make it difficult for customers to find what they need.
Weak product descriptions and low-quality images can reduce customer confidence.
Unexpected shipping charges and complicated checkout processes can contribute to abandoned carts.
Missing trust signals, unclear policies and limited payment options can make customers hesitant to purchase.
Poor SEO and technical issues can affect how easily potential customers discover your online store.
Regular website audits can help identify performance, SEO, design and usability issues.

content.text: 1. Your website takes too long to load

Website speed plays an important role in the shopping experience. When customers visit an online store, they expect product pages, images and navigation elements to load without unnecessary delays. If your website takes too long to respond, visitors may lose patience and leave before exploring your products.

Large image files, unnecessary scripts, excessive plugins, poor hosting configurations and unoptimized website code can all contribute to slow loading times. A visually attractive website may still deliver a poor experience if its pages are not optimized for performance.
How to fix it

items: Compress product images and use suitable modern image formats such as WebP.
Remove unnecessary applications, plugins and scripts.
Enable browser caching and appropriate content delivery settings.
Review your hosting and website performance configuration.
Test important pages using Google PageSpeed Insights.
Pay attention to Core Web Vitals, including loading performance, interactivity and visual stability.

content.text: Check your homepage, product pages and checkout experience separately. Improving only the homepage does not guarantee that the rest of your store will perform well.
2. Your website is not properly optimized for mobile devices

Many customers browse online stores using smartphones. If your website is difficult to navigate on a smaller screen, customers may struggle to explore products, read descriptions, select product variations or complete purchases.

Common mobile usability problems include text that is too small, buttons that are difficult to tap, images that extend beyond the screen, overlapping sections and checkout forms that are difficult to complete. These issues can make an otherwise functional website frustrating to use.
How to fix it

items: Use a responsive website design that adapts to different screen sizes.
Make navigation menus simple and easy to access.
Ensure buttons and links have comfortable touch targets.
Use readable font sizes and sufficient spacing.
Optimize images and page layouts for mobile screens.
Test the complete shopping and checkout journey on different smartphones.

content.text: Do not rely only on the desktop preview of your website. Visit your store using an actual smartphone and test it as a customer would.
3. Your website navigation is confusing

Customers should be able to find products and important information without having to search through multiple unrelated pages. Complicated navigation, poorly organized product categories and unclear menu labels can make visitors leave without discovering what your store offers.
For example, if a customer wants to purchase a particular product but cannot easily find the relevant category, they may choose another online store that offers a simpler browsing experience.
How to fix it

items: Organize products into clear and relevant categories.
Use descriptive navigation labels instead of confusing terminology.
Include a visible search option for stores with larger product catalogues.
Make important pages such as Contact, Shipping, Returns and About Us easy to access.
Avoid overcrowding the navigation menu with unnecessary links.
Keep the shopping journey consistent across desktop and mobile devices.

content.text: 4. Your product pages do not provide enough information

Product pages are among the most important sections of an eCommerce website. Customers depend on them to understand what they are buying, compare available options and decide whether a product meets their requirements.

A product page with a short generic description, missing specifications, unclear pricing or incomplete product information can leave customers with unanswered questions. This may reduce their confidence in purchasing from your store.
How to fix it

items: Write unique and informative product descriptions.
Include important specifications, dimensions, materials and compatibility details where relevant.
Clearly display pricing, discounts and product variations.
Show product availability and stock information accurately.
Add useful product images from different angles.
Include customer reviews and frequently asked questions where appropriate.
Use clear calls to action such as Add to Cart or Buy Now.

content.text: A good product page should answer the questions a customer is likely to ask before purchasing. Avoid relying entirely on manufacturer descriptions that are repeated across multiple online stores.
5. You are using poor-quality or insufficient product images
Online shoppers cannot physically examine products before purchasing. Product images therefore play an important role in helping customers understand the appearance, quality and details of an item.

Blurry photographs, inconsistent backgrounds, incorrect image proportions and missing product angles can make a store look unprofessional. Customers may also find it difficult to evaluate important product details when images do not provide enough visual information.
How to fix it

items: Use clear and high-resolution product photography.
Maintain consistent image dimensions and presentation across product listings.
Show products from multiple angles.
Include close-up images of important features and details.
Use lifestyle images where they help customers understand the product.
Optimize image file sizes without unnecessarily reducing visual quality.
Add descriptive alternative text to relevant product images.

content.text: Remember that image quality and website performance need to work together. Uploading unnecessarily large images can affect loading speed, so optimize images before publishing them.
6. Unexpected costs appear during checkout

Imagine a customer browsing your store, selecting a product and proceeding to checkout. Everything looks fine until additional shipping fees, taxes or other charges suddenly appear. The unexpected increase in the final amount may cause the customer to reconsider the purchase.
Unexpected costs are one of the common reasons customers abandon online shopping carts. Businesses should make pricing and delivery information clear before customers reach the final checkout stage.
How to fix it

items: Display shipping charges and delivery conditions clearly.
Explain applicable taxes and additional fees.
Show free shipping eligibility and minimum order requirements.
Provide estimated delivery timelines where possible.
Display the order total before customers confirm payment.
Avoid introducing unexpected charges at the final stage.

content.text: Transparent pricing helps customers make informed purchasing decisions and reduces unpleasant surprises during checkout.
7. Your checkout process is too complicated

A customer who has added a product to their cart has already shown interest in purchasing. However, a complicated checkout process can create unnecessary friction and prevent the customer from completing the order.

Long registration forms, unnecessary account creation requirements, unclear payment steps, limited payment methods and technical errors can make checkout frustrating. Customers should be able to understand what they need to do at every stage.
How to fix it

items: Keep checkout forms short and request only necessary information.
Offer guest checkout where supported and appropriate.
Provide familiar and reliable payment options.
Display clear progress indicators when checkout has multiple steps.
Make error messages understandable and actionable.
Ensure order confirmation and payment notifications work correctly.
Test successful, failed and cancelled payment scenarios.

content.text: Test the checkout process regularly, particularly after installing new plugins, apps or payment integrations. A problem that appears only during checkout can be difficult to notice if you review only the homepage.
8. Your website does not establish enough customer trust

Customers need to feel confident before sharing personal information or making payments on an unfamiliar online store. If your website lacks clear business information, contact details, policies or reliable payment information, visitors may hesitate to complete their purchases.

A professional design alone does not establish trust. Customers also look for clear information about the business, how orders are handled and what happens if a product needs to be returned or refunded.
How to fix it

items: Provide accurate business contact information.
Create clear shipping, return, refund and privacy policies.
Use HTTPS and maintain appropriate website security.
Display genuine customer reviews where available.
Explain payment methods and available customer support options.
Include an informative About Us page.
Keep business details and policy information updated.

content.text: Trust is built through transparency and consistency. Make sure the information displayed on your website accurately reflects your business operations and customer service policies.
9. Your website is not optimized for search engines

Even a well-designed online store can struggle to attract organic traffic if search engines cannot properly discover, understand and index its important pages. Poor SEO implementation can make it harder for potential customers to find your products through Google.

Common eCommerce SEO problems include missing page titles, duplicate product descriptions, poorly written meta descriptions, broken internal links, missing image alt text and incorrect indexing configurations. These issues can affect the discoverability of product and category pages.
How to fix it

items: Write unique page titles and relevant meta descriptions.
Use descriptive URLs for product and category pages.
Create useful and original product descriptions.
Organize website content using a logical heading structure.
Add relevant internal links between related products, categories and articles.
Submit an accurate XML sitemap through Google Search Console.
Check indexing, crawlability and canonical tags.
Monitor search performance and identify technical SEO issues.

content.text: SEO is an ongoing process rather than a one-time website setup task. Review your important pages regularly and make improvements based on search performance, customer behaviour and changing product information.
10. You are ignoring broken links and technical website issues

Broken links, missing images, outdated pages, malfunctioning forms and website errors can create a frustrating experience for customers. For example, a visitor may click a product link and land on a page that no longer exists, or submit an enquiry form without receiving any confirmation.

Technical issues can affect more than appearance. They may interrupt important customer journeys, reduce website usability and prevent visitors from completing actions such as purchasing a product or contacting your business.
How to fix it

items: Regularly check important website links and identify broken URLs.
Test product pages, category pages and navigation menus.
Verify that contact forms and enquiry notifications work correctly.
Monitor website errors and uptime.
Check for missing images and incorrect redirects.
Review website functionality after updates and integrations.
Keep plugins, themes and platform components maintained.

content.text: Create a routine for reviewing your website rather than waiting for customers to report problems. Regular checks can help you identify issues before they affect a larger number of visitors.
How to identify these problems on your eCommerce website
Knowing that these mistakes exist is only the first step. The next challenge is identifying which issues are actually present on your website and deciding which ones need attention first.

Start by reviewing your website from a customer's perspective. Visit your homepage, browse product categories, open product pages, add an item to your cart and test the checkout process. Check the same journey on both desktop and mobile devices.
A practical eCommerce website review checklist

items: Does your homepage load properly and communicate what your business sells?
Can visitors easily find products and important categories?
Are your product descriptions complete and informative?
Do product images display correctly on mobile and desktop?
Are shipping costs and delivery conditions easy to understand?
Can customers complete checkout without unnecessary steps?
Are your contact, shipping, return and privacy policies accessible?
Are your important pages optimized for search engines?
Are there broken links, missing images or website errors?
Are contact forms, payment methods and order notifications working?

content.text: You can also use tools such as Google PageSpeed Insights and Google Search Console to investigate website performance and search visibility. However, a complete review should also consider navigation, product information, customer trust and the overall shopping experience.

Frequently asked questions
What are the most common eCommerce website mistakes?

Some common eCommerce website mistakes include slow loading speeds, poor mobile optimization, confusing navigation, incomplete product descriptions, low-quality images, unexpected checkout costs, complicated payment processes, missing trust signals, poor SEO and unresolved technical issues.
Why is my eCommerce website getting visitors but no sales?

Visitors may leave without purchasing for several reasons, including irrelevant traffic, unclear product information, high shipping costs, poor mobile usability, slow loading speeds, limited payment options or a complicated checkout experience. Review website analytics and test the complete shopping journey to identify potential problems.
How can I improve my eCommerce website performance?

Start by optimizing images, improving page loading speed, simplifying navigation, making product information more useful, improving mobile usability and testing checkout functionality. Monitor website performance regularly and prioritize issues that affect important customer journeys.
How often should I audit my eCommerce website?

A practical approach is to review important website elements regularly and perform a more comprehensive audit periodically, such as every three to six months. You should also review the website after major design changes, platform updates, new integrations or changes to checkout and payment functionality.
Can website mistakes affect my Google rankings?

Yes, certain website problems can affect search visibility. Technical indexing issues, broken pages, poor mobile usability, slow performance and weak page content can create SEO challenges. However, search rankings depend on many factors, including content relevance, competition, site structure and overall search quality.
Can I audit my Shopify or WordPress website?

Yes. Both Shopify and WordPress websites can be reviewed for relevant SEO, performance, usability and technical issues. The specific checks available depend on the website structure, platform configuration and audit tools being used.
Is a free eCommerce website audit useful?

A free audit can be a useful starting point for identifying potential website issues and understanding areas that may need improvement. However, automated audits have limitations and may not evaluate every business requirement, customer interaction or technical problem. More detailed investigation may be required for complex issues.
Final thoughts

An eCommerce website should do more than display products. It should help customers discover products, understand their benefits, trust your business and complete purchases without unnecessary difficulty.

The ten mistakes discussed in this guide are common areas worth reviewing, but not every issue will affect every online store in the same way. Start by identifying the problems that create the greatest friction for your customers and prioritize improvements based on their impact.
